title: Variables, classes and functions should be defined before being used
description: In Python, variables, classes, and functions must be defined before they are used in the execution flow to avoid NameError exceptions. While functions and classes can be defined after their usage in some contexts due to Python's late binding, variables must always be assigned before being referenced. Using identifiers before they are defined in the execution order can lead to runtime errors and unpredictable behavior.
message: Define '{{identifier}}' before using it in the execution flow.

impact.reliability: High impact as using undefined identifiers causes NameError exceptions at runtime
impact.maintainability: Medium impact as proper ordering improves code readability and reduces confusion

recommendation: Ensure variables are assigned before being referenced, and consider moving function and class definitions before their usage for better code clarity.

references.title: SonarSource Python Rules - Variables, classes and functions should be defined before being used

noncompliant.code:
def calculate():
    result = value + 10  # NameError: 'value' used before assignment
    value = 5
    return result

noncompliant.description: Function called before definition in sequential execution
noncompliant.code:
# This will fail if executed as a script
result = helper_function()  # NameError: helper_function not defined yet

def helper_function():
    return 42

noncompliant.description: Class instantiated before definition in sequential execution
noncompliant.code:
# This will fail if executed as a script
obj = MyClass()  # NameError: MyClass not defined yet

class MyClass:
    pass

noncompliant.description: Variable referenced in loop before first assignment

noncompliant.code:
import random

if random.random() > 0.5:
    print(message)  # NameError if condition is true
    
message = "Hello World"

compliant.code:
def calculate():
    value = 5
    result = value + 10  # Variable is assigned before use
    return result

def helper_function():
    return 42

# Function is defined before use
result = helper_function()

class MyClass:
    pass

# Class is defined before use
obj = MyClass()

compliant.description: Variable assigned in all execution paths
compliant.code:
import random

message = "Default message"
if random.random() > 0.5:
    message = "Random message"
    
print(message)  # Variable is always assigned

why_is_this_an_issue: Using variables, classes, or functions before they are defined in the execution flow can lead to NameError exceptions at runtime. While Python allows forward references in some contexts (like function definitions within functions), variables must always be assigned before being referenced. This issue commonly occurs due to incorrect code ordering, conditional assignments, or misunderstanding of Python's execution model. Such errors make code unreliable and can cause program crashes.

how_to_fix.description: Identify the identifier that is being used before definition
For variables: Move the assignment statement before the first usage
For functions: Move the function definition before its first call, or restructure code to use proper function ordering
For classes: Move the class definition before its first instantiation
For conditional assignments: Ensure the variable is initialized in all possible execution paths
Consider using default values or None initialization for variables that might not be set in some code paths
Test all code paths to ensure the fix resolves the issue
